newsitem.title: POLAND: NATO entry a key Polish event in 300 years - paper.
newsitem.headline: NATO entry a key Polish event in 300 years - paper.

text.p: The Madrid summit's invitation to start talks on joining NATO counts among key events in 300 years of mostly tragic Polish history, Poland's top-selling daily, Gazeta Wyborcza, said on Wednesday.

"Poland's invitation to NATO is a breakthrough," wrote the newspaper's editor Adam Michnik, who before the 1989 fall of communism spent years in jail for his leading role in the democratic opposition.
"This day is among the most important in the last three centuries of Polish history, because fate has not treated Poles kindly for the past 300 years," Michnik wrote in a commentary.

"Poland was alone amidst enemies, it was also conquered: there were partitions, divisions, occupations," he wrote, recalling more than a century when powerful neighbours erased Poland from the map of Europe, the World War Two Nazi occupation and almost five decades of Soviet domination.
The 16 NATO countries' leaders on Tuesday invited Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary to start talks intended to lead them to membership in 1999.
Polish reactions were relieved and exultant, even though commentators underlined that a long task lay ahead to secure ratification by all 16 parliaments, requiring a major effort.

"Our fate, and that of our children and grandchildren, lies in our hands," wrote Michnik, arguing that Poland had to keep up economic growth, avoid allowing any extremism to gain ground in its own politics and cultivate ever-better ties with its neighbours -- especially Russia and Ukraine.

Rzeczpospolita, Poland's heavyweight financial daily, made similar points, focusing on the need to secure two-thirds of votes for ratification next year in the U.S. Senate where there are some doubts about the wisdom and costs of NATO enlargement.
"The invitation to the world's most powerful political-military organisation...is our great national success," its commentary said.
"What (image of) Poland will we present next year on the Capitol? Undoubtedly this depends more on ourselves than on our allies and, what is more, on our enemies," it said.

But the long-expected invitation at Madrid was not the top story in all Polish news media -- radio and television led bulletins with flooding in southern Poland, caused by rains since the weekend which have cost at least seven lives.
Warsaw's daily Zycie Warszawy gave most prominence to a report that U.S. pop star Michael Jackson may press on with plans to build a family entertainment park in the capital.
